marks.gloss_en: the same root elsewhere means strengthening, so why must Deuteronomy mean removal?
the root ח-ל-ץ can mean strengthening, as in 'He shall strengthen your bones'
the phrase me'al raglo, rather than beraglo or beme'al raglo, fixes the contextual meaning as removal
in Deuteronomy's halitza formula, the verb means removal rather than tightening
first version of Rav: even if removal was seen, do not suspect that both intended halitza
second version: observed removal without joint intent can disqualify her from the brothers, though it cannot permit her to strangers
